statement: Every negative-transposition involution in the full three-cusp loop-outer group has the global multiplier minus one. Together with D34 and D36, every involution has the global multiplier specified by its 2-adic sign, and every finite subgroup generated by involutions has the usual global orientation character.
where_proved: Part D, statement D.41; work/part_c/d41.tex; code/part_c/negative_multiplier_d41.py
depends_on: D.34; D.36; D.37; the exact finite-index completion comparison and class-two boundary pairing calculation
manuscript_passages: Part D(b) of the task; §24, folio 147 verso, scan 293; §30, folios 194–196, scans 383–387; §31, folios 198–199 verso, scans 391–394.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The cyclic cover, two cusp fillings, deck extension, Schreier generators and boundary word are all given by exact presentation maps.
notes: At a least odd prime q with positive multiplier, the cyclic q-cover with cusp monodromies (-2,1,1) fills equivariantly to genus (q-1)/2 with one boundary. Its deck module is the multiplicity-one cyclotomic module. For a prime divisor p of q-1 having even order modulo q, every local cyclotomic summand is self-dual; a commuting involution acts as a scalar sign and must have symplectic multiplier plus one at p. Minimality of q makes that multiplier minus one, a contradiction. The statement determines multipliers and does not assert finite-action conjugacy.
